title: President Jeremiah John Rawlings of Ghana has announced that he will not seek re-election in 2000, endorsing his vice president, Professor John E Atta-Mills, as his successor. This announcement was made during a rally commemorating the 19th anniversary of his first coup. Rawlings, who has been in power for nearly 20 years, expressed confidence in Atta-Mills' ability to continue the National Democratic Congress's policies aimed at economic reconstruction and social development. Atta-Mills, a former law professor and IRS commissioner, is seen as a moderate who appeals to the middle class and business community. The announcement came shortly before the unexpected death of Nigerian leader General Sani Abacha, whom Rawlings praised as a nationalist. Atta-Mills has already begun to call for unity with opposition parties as he prepares for the upcoming elections.
